result.title: Role-Adaptive Policy Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Policy regularization in offline reinforcement learning balances policy improvement against reliance on uncertain value estimates. This balance can differ between selecting actions for execution and supplying actions for critic bootstrapping, yet methods such as TD3+BC couple these roles through a shared policy. We propose Role-Adaptive Policy Optimization (RAPO), which adapts policy-update coefficients according to their roles in value learning and execution. RAPO learns these coefficients by differentiating through candidate policy updates formed using the base algorithm's actor objective. For TD3+BC, RAPO separates bootstrap and execution actors and adapts their coefficients independently: the bootstrap objective penalizes policy-induced changes in target values, while the execution objective evaluates a local policy-improvement surrogate. For IQL, whose value learning is already independent of the execution actor, RAPO preserves the original value updates and adapts only the inverse temperature in advantage-weighted policy extraction. Experiments on D4RL locomotion and AntMaze tasks show improvements over both base algorithms, with larger gains for TD3+BC, whose RAPO instantiation outperforms baselines on average.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 Role-Adaptive Policy Optimization（RAPO），在离线强化学习中按策略在价值学习（bootstrap）与执行中的不同角色，分别自适应调节策略更新系数，并在 TD3+BC 与 IQL 上实例化，D4RL 任务上取得提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同一策略在 bootstrap 与执行中承担不同角色、需分别加权」的思路，可能启发 LVR 中 latent 状态对价值/评论家训练与最终答案生成的贡献分配与监督设计，但联系较远，可供核查。
